_comment: NativeIntempt.ts is excluded because it is a type-only TurboModule spec — an
interface plus a TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing call. There is no behaviour
to mutate, and its contents are checked by check-corpus.mjs against the
contract instead.
break is 95, set AFTER measuring rather than aspirationally. The suite scored
77.67 on its first run at 99% statement coverage, which is the whole argument
for mutation testing: every surviving mutant was on a line the tests already
executed. It is now 97.57.
TWO MUTANTS ARE EQUIVALENT AND WILL NEVER DIE. Chasing them would mean writing
tests that assert nothing:
Located by CODE, not by line number. The previous version of this comment cited
src/index.ts:66 and src/errors.ts:77, and both had drifted to a different line —
a stale pointer in the justification for the score ceiling is worse than none.
src/index.ts, encodeValue()'s `value !== null && typeof value === 'object'`
— typeof null === 'object', so the mutant calls
encodeProperties(null), which returns null. Identical output by
a different route.
src/errors.ts, IntemptError's constructor `Object.setPrototypeOf` call
— only load-bearing when transpiled to ES5. This build
targets esnext, where instanceof works without it. The line
stays for consumers who do target ES5.
So the practical ceiling here is ~99, not 100.
concurrency is 2 deliberately. Stryker counts a TIMED-OUT mutant as KILLED, so
a machine competing with its own test runs inflates the score and the inflation
is indistinguishable from progress. 4 mutants time out on this machine even at
2 workers, so the honest score excluding them is 197/206 = 95.6, not 97.57.
